There are instances where the States have not provided necessary protection for non-migratory endangered species that occur within their borders. Under the proposed legislation, it would be unlawful to take species or subspecies presently threatened with extinction except for scientific, educational and propagational purposes or in hardship cases within one year after listing.

However, the Secretary may, upon determination that the State maintains an effective program for a species or subspecies threatened with extinction, delegate to the State authority for management and protection of those species. The proposed legislation also gives the Secretary authority to issue regulations for the management and protection of species and subspecies which are likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction.
The proposed legislation provides for Federal protection of endangered species not only on the territorial lands and waters of the United States but also protects endangered animals on the high seas from any person subject to the jurisdiction of the United States.
Present authority requires separate endangered species lists for native and foreign species and subspecies. The proposed legislation omits any distinction between native and foreign species.
Present authority provides a "hardship clause" that allows the Secretary to permit importation of a species or subspecies for up to a year after it is declared endangered provided the person allegedly harmed can prove that he will suffer undue economic hardship and has a valid contract which was valid at the time the animal was listed as endangered.
